arguments.name: ext
arguments.text: Extension to test for, without the leading dot.

origin.details: Compares tools::file_ext(path) with ext. Only a trailing alphanumeric extension is recognized. The manual example does not call has_extension, so this page adds that call.
origin.example:
see_if(is.dir(1))

tmp <- tempfile()
see_if(file.exists(tmp))
see_if(is.dir(tmp))

writeLines("x", tmp)
see_if(file.exists(tmp))
see_if(is.dir(tmp))
see_if(is.writeable(tmp))
see_if(is.readable(tmp))
unlink(tmp)

see_if(is.readable(tmp))

see_if(has_extension("dir/foo.bar", "txt"))

arguments.name: ext
arguments.text: Extension to test for, without the leading dot.

translation.details: Compares tools.file_ext with ext. Only a trailing alphanumeric extension is recognized. The character class is libc iswalnum.
translation.example:
import os
import tempfile

from assertthat import see_if

print(see_if("is.dir(1)"))

tmp = os.path.join(tempfile.gettempdir(), f"assertthat-example-{os.getpid()}")
if os.path.exists(tmp):
    os.remove(tmp)
print(see_if("file.exists(tmp)"))
print(see_if("is.dir(tmp)"))

with open(tmp, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
    handle.write("x\n")
print(see_if("file.exists(tmp)"))
print(see_if("is.dir(tmp)"))
print(see_if("is.writeable(tmp)"))
print(see_if("is.readable(tmp)"))
os.remove(tmp)

print(see_if("is.readable(tmp)"))

print(see_if('has_extension("dir/foo.bar", "txt")'))
